title: Toward High-Performance Blockchain System by Blurring the Line between Ordering and Execution
problem: Blockchain execution has become the primary bottleneck after advances in DAG-based consensus, and current systems that segregate execution from ordering fail to exploit parallelism available in transaction batches.
motivation: With consensus no longer limiting throughput (100k+ TPS), optimizing transaction execution is critical for improving overall blockchain system performance.
method: OptME figures out which transactions can run in parallel while still producing the same final result as if they had run one after another in a predetermined order. It does this by analyzing which transactions depend on each other (by tracking which ones read or write the same data), creating a schedule that runs non-conflicting transactions simultaneously, and executing them according to that plan. To speed this up, it analyzes dependencies in parallel, stops transactions early if they conflict, and uses optimistic reordering—assuming transactions will succeed and rearranging them for speed, then rolling back if a conflict is discovered.
key_novelty: By analyzing which transactions depend on each other, you can find which ones can run in parallel while maintaining the correct predetermined order—doing both simultaneously instead of as separate phases.
contributions: OptME algorithm for deterministic concurrency control with transaction-level parallelism extraction
Parallel dependency graph construction and schedule generation techniques
Early abort detection and optimistic reordering optimizations
Demonstration achieving 350k TPS outperforming state-of-the-art concurrency control algorithms

metrics.other: outperforms state-of-the-art concurrency control algorithm even under high contention

primary_theme: blockchain throughput optimization via transaction-level parallelism
